newsitem.title: LEBANON: Byblos Bank to raise share capital to $130 mln.
newsitem.headline: Byblos Bank to raise share capital to $130 mln.

text.p: The board of Lebanon's Byblos Bank has decided to increase share capital to 200 billion Lebanese pounds from 66 billion and will present the proposal to shareholders for approval on June 12, a bank official said.

The board intends to delay the planned listing of 30 percent of the bank's shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange until the capital increase is concluded, possibly in late September, the official told Reuters.
"We expected to be listed in May but we have postponed this to increase capital. Maybe the listing will be in late September. Maybe," the official said.
Byblos is one of Lebanon's most dynamic banks and its listing is eagerly awaited on the re-emerging Beirut Stock Exchange. Its shares have quadrupled on the parallel market in the past two years.

The increase in share capital, to be put to an extraordinary shareholders meeting on June 12, would be carried out by issuing new shares for existing shareholders to contribute to, the official said. The managers of the issue had not yet been appointed, he added.
The increase is part of a programme to raise Byblos' capitalisation to $200 million within 18 months announced by Chairman Francois Bassile in February.
A bank spokesman told Reuters the current increase would bring total capitalisation to about $160 million.
Byblos' listing was originally planned for the start of the year but was delayed due to the need to meet a legal requirement that 33 percent of its shares remain in Lebanese hands after listing.

To do this the bank is creating a new Lebanese-based holding company. This will be 50 percent owned by Lebanese and will hold 30 percent of the bank's A shares which are restricted to Lebanese citizens, the official said.
"We are in the process of forming the holding company. We have the approval of the central bank and hope it will be done by the end of May," he said.
